standard.title: First Nations media arts and culture
standard.description: explore ways First Nations Australians use media arts to continue and revitalise cultures
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explain how First Nations Australians use media arts to communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place, and can compare multiple works across forms. They have not yet explored how media arts works are used specifically to continue and revitalise cultures — or investigated how cultural expressions change over time.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore ways First Nations Australians use media arts to continue and revitalise cultures, including how media artists embed community identity and how cultural expressions change over time.

nodes.label: Media arts for cultural continuity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how and why First Nations Australian media arts works are critical for sharing, maintaining, continuing and revitalising cultures.
nodes.minimum_width: Explore one First Nations Australian media arts work and explain at least one specific way it contributes to sharing, maintaining or revitalising culture.
nodes.typical_width: Explore how and why First Nations Australian cultural expressions and media arts works are critical for cultural continuity; investigate specific examples using community-published resources; discuss what is communicated and what would be lost if these works were not made; engage with accredited First Nations Australian resources.
wider: Using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australian organisations, investigate how and why cultural expressions are shared and maintained through media arts — discussing specific examples and what would be at risk if these forms were not continued

Explore how First Nations Australian media arts works created for different purposes (language maintenance, ceremonial recording, community storytelling, popular culture) each contribute differently to cultural continuity
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding the cultural continuity function of First Nations Australian media arts is the conceptual foundation for this standard — without it, analysis of specific representations (identity, visibility, change over time) has no grounding.

response_modes.reason: Students need guided inquiry with community-published resources to understand cultural continuity — Viewpoints questions help: 'What do I already know about this issue?', 'Is there more to this story than is being presented?'

success_criteria: Student can explain at least one way a First Nations Australian media arts work contributes to sharing, maintaining or revitalising culture
Student grounds their explanation in specific features of the work (not general statements about First Nations culture)

nodes.label: Identity, visibility and change over time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how First Nations Australian media artists embed community identity in works and how cultural expressions change over time.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one example of a First Nations Australian media artist embedding community identity in a work (e.g. representing their community as superheroes, protagonists, or central storytellers) and explain what this communicates.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists embed themselves and their communities in works as declarations of identity, storytelling and resilience; examine how cultural expressions have changed over time using archived and contemporary works; discuss specific examples from comics, popular culture and television.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists represent their communities as superheroes or protagonists in comics, popular culture and television — examining these as visual declarations of identity, resilience and storytelling, and discussing what changes when First Nations communities are central rather than peripheral

Compare archived First Nations Australian media arts works with contemporary works on the same theme — identifying what has been maintained, what has evolved, and what forces (technological, social, political) have shaped the changes

response_modes.reason: Vary the examples — comics, television, online media, archived and contemporary — to ensure students encounter the genuine breadth of First Nations Australian media arts practice, not a single representative example.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of forms and periods in which First Nations Australian media artists have embedded community identity (comics, TV, online, animation, archived vs contemporary) is genuinely rich for exploration — breadth produces much more accurate and respectful understanding.
success_criteria: Student can identify at least one example of a First Nations Australian media artist embedding community identity in a work
Student can explain what this communicates about identity, resilience or cultural continuity
